description: Cross a rare bridge chapel, meet the town’s Victorian traders and find the public statue that remembers Cromwell’s five years in St Ives.
author: Day Tripping Quiz

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A tiny place of prayer rides the bridge above the river’s flow.
stops.Hint_1: Walk to the medieval bridge across the Great Ouse.
stops.Hint_2: Find the small stone chapel built into the bridge itself.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The St Leger bridge chapel was completed in 1426 as part of St Ives Bridge. It is one of four surviving medieval bridge chapels in England and once served travellers through prayer and toll collection.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From a safe point on the bridge, identify one feature that makes the chapel look like a tiny church.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Victorian merchants raised this grand hall so grain could be traded and townspeople could gather.
stops.Hint_1: Head into the centre and look for an imposing public building on The Pavement.
stops.Hint_2: Find the Corn Exchange, opened in 1864.
stops.Unlock_Fact: St Ives Corn Exchange opened in 1864, funded by local businessmen for corn trading, concerts and public meetings. Residents later campaigned to save it, and it reopened as a community venue in 2010.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Look for one decorative detail in the Italianate frontage and describe its colour or shape.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: A bronze farmer with sword and Bible remembers five local years before national power.
stops.Hint_1: Search Market Hill for a standing bronze figure.
stops.Hint_2: Find the 1901 statue of Oliver Cromwell.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Oliver Cromwell lived in St Ives from 1631 to 1636. F. W. Pomeroy’s statue was unveiled in 1901 after a public fundraising campaign and portrays Cromwell as a country gentleman.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Without stepping into traffic, identify the two objects held by the statue.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Follow Cromwell’s name from bronze to a former brewery near the old riverport.
stops.Hint_1: Leave Market Hill for Wellington Street near the quayside.
stops.Hint_2: Find the pub named The Oliver Cromwell.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The Oliver Cromwell began as the Feathers brewery in the early 1800s and took its present name in 1876, chosen by a republican-minded landlord’s son. Stop for food or a drink if it is open.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Look for one exterior detail that refers either to Cromwell or the building’s brewing past.

short_description: A compact riverport trail of medieval devotion, market trade and Cromwell.

before_you_go.terrain: Market-town pavements, the historic bridge approach and short riverside streets, with occasional uneven surfaces.
before_you_go.hills: Largely level apart from the gentle rise over St Ives Bridge.
before_you_go.steps: No steps are required to solve the exterior clues; entry to individual buildings is not part of the route.
before_you_go.accessibility: The medieval bridge can be narrow and busy, and old paving may be uneven. Check local access updates if step-free travel is essential.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current town-centre, bus-station or museum facility listings before departure.
before_you_go.footwear: Comfortable shoes are suitable; grip helps when the bridge and quayside are wet.
before_you_go.dogs: Outdoor route; keep dogs under control and check the finishing venue’s current dog policy before entering.
before_you_go.pushchairs: The route is compact but the historic bridge and crowded market area may require patience.

recommended_age: Recommended 8+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A short, mostly level circuit around the historic bridge, Market Hill and quayside streets.
